question: What is the main purpose of maintaining dissolved oxygen in an aeration basin?
correctAnswer: To support aerobic microorganisms that oxidize organic matter and ammonia
explanation: Aerobic microorganisms need dissolved oxygen to oxidize organic matter and, where nitrification occurs, ammonia. Oxygen does not sterilize mixed liquor or replace preliminary treatment.
options: To support aerobic microorganisms that oxidize organic matter and ammonia
To sterilize the mixed liquor before clarification
To prevent any solids from settling in the secondary clarifier
To remove grit and screenings from the influent
sourceTitle: US EPA: Municipal Wastewater — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Advanced activated sludge control. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: To support aerobic microorganisms that oxidize organic matter and ammonia
optionB: To sterilize the mixed liquor before clarification
optionC: To prevent any solids from settling in the secondary clarifier
optionD: To remove grit and screenings from the influent

options: The outlet probe is the only probe that can be trusted

The influent has already been fully treated before aeration

To let microorganisms use nitrate as an oxygen source and convert it to nitrogen gas
To settle solids ahead of the aeration basin
